test.title: Why bread went stale more slowly

paragraphs.text: Bakers have known for centuries that bread kept in a cold place dries out faster than bread left on the table. For a long time nobody could explain why cold air, which slows down most spoiling, made bread worse.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The answer lies in starch. As bread cools, starch molecules slowly rearrange themselves into a firmer structure, and this happens fastest at temperatures just above freezing. The bread is not drying out; it is changing shape inside.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: This is why a loaf in the freezer stays soft for weeks: below freezing the molecules can hardly move at all. Bakers now advise customers to freeze bread they cannot eat within a day, and to warm slices before serving.
paragraphs.label: C
